summary: Boise National Forest lookout first built in 1927; the current flat cab on a concrete base dates to 1979 or 1981 and is staffed in fire season.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 10-foot concrete base

access.note: Staffed drive-up lookout on the Boise National Forest. The sources do not describe public visits.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as drive-up. The 1927 account describes a trail as the only road up or down, so ask the Boise National Forest about current access.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Boise National Forest

events.note: First lookout, a two-story log structure. The register says it was similar to a California Plan 4A.
Photo evidence suggests it was raised onto a 10-foot log base, per firelookout.com.
Earliest known staff listed by Idaho Fire Lookouts (1962-1963).
The register gives 1979 for the current two-story structure.
Flat cab on a 10-foot concrete base, per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The Forest Lookouts history page gives 1981 for a two-story flat roof house.
Lookout threatened by the Willis Gulch fire along with a nearby private subdivision.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 28, 2020.
Roger Lockwood listed as known staff.

corrections.why: Sources give a 10-foot concrete base, not an overall tower height. The 3.0 m figure is the base alone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1979 for the current two-story structure. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1981 for a flat cab. The Forest Lookouts history page gives 1981 for a two-story flat roof house.
The register calls the current structure two-story. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe a flat cab on a concrete base. The record lists two_story, so the story describes both.
The register gives 8,119 ft. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 8124 ft.

notes_for_editor: The 1927 quote comes from the Forest Lookouts transcription of the Idaho Statesman, not the paper itself. Staffing as of 2020 is from the register, and Idaho Fire Lookouts names a 2025 staffer. The register and firelookout.com disagree on whether the current structure is one or two stories. The record height of 3.0 m is the 10-foot concrete base, not a tower height.
